turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the last token of a line, the token right before a newline. This holds across YAML values, code lines ending in `{` or `;`, license and comment lines, headings, and sentences that end a paragraph.
turn1.evidence: Nearly every marked token sits at a line end: `1`/`0` in the YAML config, `{` after method signatures, `Coder`/`info` before a newline, `Book` and `Invention` at the end of title lines, and the surname endings in the race-results list. Tokens in the middle of a line stay unmarked even when they are punctuation or the same kind of word.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on the same text with the line breaks removed or moved would confirm the unit is predicting a newline rather than responding to the content at the end of a line. Mid-line contexts (e.g. the `but` in middle example 5) would also show whether it fires on clause ends in running text.
